cards.title: Diagnose inflated ROAS in Advantage+ scaling campaigns with audience breakdowns
cards.summary: Break a top-spending Advantage+ TOF ad down by audience (new vs existing vs engaged) to reveal when headline ROAS is really just retargeting existing customers.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a Meta Advantage+ top-of-funnel scaling campaign where a top-spending ad shows a very high platform ROAS and you need to decide whether to scale budget, brief more creative like it, or pull spend.
steps: Start with the ad-level report sorted by spend. High frequency on the top ad is the first red flag — the source flags this as a symptom of retargeting-style delivery, not genuine TOF reach.

Open the audience breakdown (existing customers / engaged / new) and read how spend distributes across segments. In the source example, roughly half of the budget on a 'scaling' campaign was landing on existing customers.

Re-read ROAS within the new-audience segment only. The source example dropped from a 13x blended ROAS to about 5x on new audiences — still positive, but a different decision than the headline implied.

Use the gap between blended ROAS and new-customer ROAS as the diagnostic: a large gap means the ad set is over-distributing spend because it performs well on existing customers, not because the creative is a strong acquisition asset.

Do not brief more creative in that format or 'double down' on that concept until the breakdown confirms new-customer performance, because scaling a fake winner adds creative production cost against bad data.
Verify the current Meta Ads Manager interface for where audience breakdowns live — column layouts and breakdown menus change.
caveats: Percentages and the 13x-to-5x drop are one account example, not a benchmark; run your own breakdown.
A high frequency is a yellow flag, not proof — check it against the audience breakdown before acting.

cards.title: Use 7-day click for optimization and treat incremental attribution as a breakout only
cards.summary: Optimize Meta campaigns on 7-day click (ignore view-throughs) and use Meta's incremental attribution only as a comparison column, because it is a modelled estimate, not a holdout result.
cards.use_when: Setting the attribution/optimization setting on any Meta cold or scaling campaign, or deciding whether to switch optimization toward incremental attribution because it looks 'more accurate'.
steps: Set the attribution setting for optimization to 7-day click, ignoring view-throughs, so that ad-level spend distribution follows conversions actually caused by a click.
Add incremental attribution as a comparison column (via the compare-attribution-settings view) rather than as the optimization target.

Understand what incremental attribution is before trusting it: per the source, it applies a factor derived from aggregated competitor lift studies to your account — it is an algorithmic estimate, not a measurement of your customers.

Contrast that with a true Meta Conversion Lift Test, which is a geo-holdout difference-in-difference experiment: Meta holds out a percentage of the target audience, compares conversion rates between held-out and served groups, and the difference is the true incremental lift.
Use a lift test when you genuinely need to know incremental impact; use incremental attribution only as directional context when ordering your ad-level analysis.
Confirm current names of these settings inside the Experiments and column-customization menus, as Meta relabels them over time.
caveats: The source's position (do not optimize toward incremental attribution) is an opinion with a stated reason, not a universal rule; a lift test is the recommended ground-truth substitute.
Incremental attribution's exact modelling method is not disclosed by Meta, so its accuracy for your category is unverifiable.

cards.title: Exclude existing customers from cold TOF campaigns, with a lapsed-customer carve-out
cards.summary: Block existing customers from cold scaling campaigns so spend cannot cannibalize retargeting, but segment long-lapsed buyers into their own campaign rather than hard-excluding them.
cards.use_when: Structuring a Meta cold/prospecting or Advantage+ top-of-funnel campaign and defining exclusion audiences, especially when attempting to scale and new-customer acquisition is flat while CAC rises.
steps: Add an existing-customer exclusion to every cold top-of-funnel scaling campaign, so budget cannot flow to people already in your customer file.

Decide a recency threshold for 'existing'. The source suggests roughly a 2-year window as a reasonable starting point: someone who last purchased two years ago is treated as lapsed rather than active.

Do not simply hard-exclude lapsed customers with the same logic as recent buyers. Give them a dedicated campaign and dedicated strategy so they get some spend without contaminating cold acquisition data.
Keep acquisition (cold) spend separate from retargeting spend so retargeting performance is not propped up by cold-campaign cannibalization, and cold performance is not propped up by past buyers.

When CAC climbs on every scaling attempt while new-customer acquisition stays flat, check this structure first — the source identifies unexcluded existing customers as a primary cause of that pattern.
Verify the current interface for customer-list exclusion setup in Meta, as the exclusions UI changes.
caveats: The 2-year threshold is a source heuristic, not a tested constant; choose a window that reflects your repurchase cycle.
Some categories have short repurchase cycles where a shorter lapse window is appropriate — test rather than copy the number.

cards.title: Measure scaling lift on top-line new-customer sales at the SKU level
cards.summary: Validate a TOF scaling campaign against top-line revenue (ideally new-customer sales on a specific SKU) rather than accepting in-platform ROAS as the success metric.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a Meta TOF scaling campaign actually worked after a budget increase, or when total-revenue-based readouts are too noisy to reach significance in a reasonable test window.
steps: Check whether the campaign concentrates on one SKU or a small SKU set. If it does, read sales for that specific SKU before and after the scale-up instead of relying on store-wide totals.

Prefer this SKU-level readout because a whole-store test needs either a much larger budget change or a much longer duration to reach statistical relevance — narrowing to one SKU raises signal per dollar of spend.
Further narrow to new-customer sales on that SKU, since the stated objective of an Advantage+ TOF scaling campaign is acquiring new customers, not re-acquiring existing ones.
Compare in-platform reported ROAS against this Shopify-side new-customer SKU sales movement; divergence means platform attribution is overstating the campaign's acquisition contribution.
Confirm the SKU was not simultaneously promoted elsewhere (other channels, promotions, email) so the revenue movement can plausibly be attributed to the scaling change.
Recheck Shopify reporting views and any current Meta reporting fields, since both interfaces change.
caveats: The source example only notes that sales 'might have gone up' — it does not report a confirmed lift, so treat this as method, not evidence of results.
SKU-level readout works best when scaling a single SKU; for large SKU-count campaigns, isolate the SKU under test explicitly.

cards.title: Why optimizing on 1-day view-through inflates rankings and misallocates spend
cards.summary: If the ad set optimizes on 7-day click plus 1-day view, spend concentrates on view-through-heavy ads, so the in-platform ranking of your best creatives is not trustworthy.
cards.use_when: Interpreting ad-level performance rankings in a Meta scaling campaign, or deciding which creative concepts to brief more of based on which ads are winning inside the account.
steps: Check whether the ad set's optimization/attribution includes 1-day view. If it does, an ad can accumulate spend from view-throughs rather than click-caused purchases.

Recognize the loop: the ad set allocates spend to ads that 'perform' including viewers, sometimes on existing customers, so those ads rank top and receive more budget — not because they acquire new customers.

Treat every ad ranking in such an account as untrustworthy, and consider that a lower-spend ad may actually be the best new-audience performer because spend was never distributed to it in line with new-customer performance.
Before briefing more creative in the 'winning' format, switch optimization to 7-day click, exclude existing customers, and re-read the rankings.
Watch for the downstream cost: teams commission more of a format based on bad rankings, adding creative and operating expense against a concept that was never validated.
Confirm the current attribution-setting options in Meta Ads Manager before applying this.
caveats: View-through conversions are not inherently worthless; the source's argument is that they should not drive optimization decisions in a cold acquisition campaign.
This is a diagnostic reasoning chain from the source, illustrated with one account rather than a controlled study.

cards.title: Read purchase conversion separately from lead conversion when auditing a scaling campaign
cards.summary: Keep purchase-based campaign metrics distinct from lead-based ones, since the diagnosis of an inflated scaling campaign depends on conversions that end in sales, not leads.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a Meta cold acquisition campaign that runs on purchase events, or when a campaign's reported performance differs depending on whether leads or purchases are counted.
steps: Confirm the campaign's optimization event is purchase, not lead, before applying the click-vs-view and new-vs-existing diagnoses — a lead-optimized ad set can look incremental while adding little revenue.
If the business collects leads that convert to purchase off-platform, split reporting: platform ROAS will only capture the lead event, while true acquisition performance lives in the CRM or store.
For purchase-optimized TOF scaling, apply the full diagnostic chain: audience breakdown, then attribution-setting comparison, then SKU-level new-customer sales in Shopify.
Do not compare a lead-based conversion rate to a purchase-based conversion rate when judging the same campaign; they measure different stages.
State which conversion type a benchmark refers to when relaying results, since the source's ROAS discussion is explicitly about purchase conversions in a scaling campaign.
Check current campaign objective and event options in Meta, as these are periodically renamed.
caveats: The source discusses purchase-based scaling campaigns specifically; it does not provide separate guidance on lead-gen diagnostics.
Conversion event choice is set at campaign creation and changing it later resets learning — plan structure before launch.

cards.title: Diagnostic path when CAC rises on every scaling attempt and new customers stay flat
cards.summary: When scale-ups raise CAC without raising new-customer acquisition, run a fixed three-check audit: retargeting overlap, over-attribution, and cold-spend cannibalization.
cards.use_when: A store repeatedly increases Meta budget and sees CAC climb while new-customer count stays flat, and you need a structured first-pass audit of the ad account.
steps: Check for retargeting: break the scaling campaign's spend down by audience to see how much is going to existing customers or engaged users.
Check for over-attribution: compare 7-day click versus view-through and versus incremental attribution on the same ads to see whether reported ROAS rests on view-throughs or modelled factors.

Check for cannibalization: confirm cold top-of-funnel campaigns are not outbidding or absorbing audiences that retargeting campaigns should be serving, which inflates retargeting's apparent success and hides cold performance.
Fix the structure first — 7-day click optimization, existing-customer exclusions on cold campaigns — before drawing conclusions from any ad-level ranking.
Then measure the scaling effort on top-line new-customer sales at the SKU level, since in-platform ROAS is the metric that was misleading to begin with.
Re-audit after changes, because correcting attribution shifts which ads win spend and changes the rankings you were relying on.
caveats: The source presents this as a reasoning framework, illustrated by an account where scaling had repeatedly raised CAC — not a tested remedy with published outcomes.
The source's claim that most accounts skip these basics is its own observation, not a measured statistic.

11-ADC / ad copy and deployment

Goes here. Ad account structure, budget distribution, scaling rules, attribution modeling, return on ad spend (ROAS) targets, incrementality testing parameters, Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) tolerance, and evaluating unit economics on first vs. returning customers.

Not here.

Ad creative formats, concepts, aesthetic guidelines, video overlays, or evaluating ad creative quality -> 10-MCR

Google Analytics reporting or general marketing mix modeling (MMM) tools -> 06-MEA

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details how to diagnose flawed ROAS metrics in Meta ad accounts by utilizing audience breakdowns and attribution windows, demonstrating that top-spending ads often over-index on retargeting returning customers and view-through conversions rather than driving incremental new customer acquisition. modules: [ADC] topics: [attribution and modeling, campaign setup and tracking] tier: 2 scope_hint: core

Topics. attribution and modeling / Deconstructing deceptive Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) metrics within Meta Advantage+ campaigns by demonstrating how a seemingly strong 13x ROAS often masks poor performance (e.g., a 1.7x incremental ROAS) once analyzed through the lens of audience breakdowns (existing vs. new customers) and attribution settings (7-day click vs. 1-day view). Differentiating between a true Conversion Lift Test (a geo-holdout experiment based on difference-in-difference design) and Meta's "incremental attribution" setting (an algorithmic estimate based on aggregated competitor data), advising against using the latter for campaign optimization. campaign setup and tracking / Establishing strict account structure guidelines to prevent top-of-funnel scaling campaigns from cannibalizing retargeting audiences. Mandating the use of a 7-day click attribution setting for optimization (ignoring view-throughs) and explicitly excluding existing customers from cold campaigns (with specific nuances for lapsed customers, e.g., excluding 2-year purchasers). Recommending that scaling efforts be measured against top-line revenue impact—specifically, new customer sales at the individual SKU level—rather than relying solely on in-platform ROAS.

Look for. The primary reason a top-spending ad in an Advantage+ campaign might actually be performing poorly: it is over-allocating budget to existing customers and relying heavily on 1-day view-through conversions rather than driving incremental new customers. The recommended attribution setting for campaign optimization: 7-day click. The distinction between a Meta Conversion Lift Test and Meta's "incremental attribution" setting: a lift test is a true holdout experiment, whereas the incremental setting is merely an algorithmic estimate based on competitor averages. The primary method to verify ad scaling success: measuring top-line new customer sales at the specific SKU level in Shopify.

Skip. General complaints about other agencies misinterpreting data.

Scope mix. Almost all core.

Volume. 5 to 10.
